 Cancer Council ACT marks 45 years of Slip! Slop! Slap! by encouraging sun-safe habits that last a lifetime
 Cancer Council ACT
 3 mins read
 3 mins read 
 Little Sid Seagull lands in Canberra to help a new generation stay SunSmart. 
 As Australia marks National Skin Cancer Action Week (NSCAW) from 15 – 22 November, Cancer Council ACT is encouraging Canberrans to build sun-safe habits that last a lifetime, with the return of beloved sun safety icon Sid Seagull and a renewed focus on protecting generations now and into the future from skin cancer. This year marks 45 years since Australians first met Sid Seagull through the iconic Slip! Slop! Slap! Campaign. 
 Cancer Council ACT CEO, Verity Hawkins, said while progress has been made, skin cancer remains one of Australia's most common cancers, with 2 in 3 Australians diagnosed with skin cancer during their lifetime. 
 "Forty-five years on, Sid's message is just as important today as it was when Australians first heard it," Ms Hawkins said. 
 "This year's theme, Sun Safe Habits Last a Lifetime , is about helping people build simple habits that become part of their everyday routine, whether they're at school, work, exercising outdoors or spending time with family and friends." 
 This is especially important in the nation’s capital, as ABS research shows that 70% of ACT residents are outdoors during peak UV times - higher than the national average. 
 Through its SunSmart program, Cancer Council ACT works with schools and early childhood education services across Canberra to create environments that support sun protection and help children establish healthy habits from an early age. As of February 2026, over 40,000 ACT children are being protected from harmful UV rays by attending SunSmart schools and early learning centres. 
 "We know the earlier children learn sun-safe habits, the more likely they are to continue them throughout their lives. Parents, carers, educators and sporting organisations all play an important role in modelling those behaviours." Ms Hawkins shared. 
 Cancer Council ACT is encouraging Canberrans to check daily UV levels and remember the five forms of sun protection when the UV Index is 3 or above, or when spending extended time outdoors: Slip on protective clothing, Slop on SPF50 or SPF50+ sunscreen, Slap on a hat, Seek shade and Slide on sunglasses. 
 Local running group TTS is also encouraging sun-safe behaviours among its members. They hold an annual fundraising run to raise awareness of the importance of being SunSmart while running. 
 "There's a strong connection between running and skin cancer prevention”, Brian from TTS said. "As runners, we spend a great deal of time outdoors, so we're particularly conscious of the importance of sunscreen, hats and protective clothing." 
 This year the fundraising run will be in NSCAW, on 21 November. For the last six years, they have raised more than $5000 annually. These funds helps Cancer Council ACT empower the community to reduce their cancer risk through prevention and education programs. 
 To celebrate the 45-year anniversary, local ACT primary schools and early learning centres can go in the draw to win a NSCAW SunSmart pack for their school, including limited edition Little Sid Seagull plushies, by renewing their SunSmart membership. Contact the Cancer Council ACT SunSmart team at [email protected] to learn more. 
 -ENDS-   
 Notes to editors: 
 About our SunSmart program 
 SunSmart is a skin cancer prevention program that aims to reduce the incidence and impact of skin cancer in the ACT. 
 Cancer Council ACT provides leadership in skin cancer prevention and early detection through the SunSmart program via community engagement, education, multi-media campaigns and advocacy in early childhood, school, and workplace settings. 
 The National SunSmart Schools and Early Childhood Program aims to reduce harmful exposure to UV radiation of students and staff by promoting awareness around sun protection, skin damage and skin cancer risks and encouraging development of effective policies on shade and sun protection measures at education facilities.  
 SunSmart status is awarded to registered primary schools and early learning centres across the ACT who have committed to implementing a school sun protection policy and meet SunSmart criteria. 
 About TTS Fundraising Run 
 The annual TTS Fundraising Run and Breakfast is organised by Brian Jones and the TTS Running Club at Pine Island in Canberra. 
 Each year, the event brings runners and supporters together to raise funds for Cancer Council ACT through our Do It For Cancer fundraising platform. 
 The event regularly raises more than $5,000 annually, over the last 6 years of fundraising, Brian and the TTS community have raised more than $30,000 for Cancer Council ACT. 
 Brian's event is a great reminder that fundraising doesn't need to fit a particular mould. Through Do It For Cancer, supporters can create an event that reflects their interests, skills or community. 
 Whether it's a fun run, trivia night, garage sale, head shave, morning tea or asking for donations in lieu of gifts, every fundraiser helps fund life-saving cancer research and vital support services. 
 If you are interested in creating your own Do It For Cancer fundraising event you can head to the website: doitforcancer.com.au or get in touch with our team and they can help set up a page. 
About us: About Cancer Council ACT: 
 Cancer Council ACT has been advocating for Canberrans living with cancer for 50 years across every aspect of cancer prevention, support and research to alleviate the impact of cancer in the community. Learn more about what we do here.
